title: Formal smoothness for an adic topology is stable under base change
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $\mathfrak n\subseteq S$ an ideal such that $S$ is formally smooth over $R$ for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Let $R\to R'$ be any homomorphism of commutative rings, $S'=S\otimes_RR'$ [def-weil-module-base-change] (a commutative ring, and an $R'$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] via $r'\mapsto1\otimes r'$) and $\mathfrak n'=\mathfrak nS'$ the ideal of $S'$ generated by the image of $\mathfrak n$ under $s\mapsto s\otimes1$. Then $S'$ is formally smooth over $R'$ for the $\mathfrak n'$-adic topology.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07EG (lemma-base-change-fs, line 9346) and its proof (universal property of the tensor product)

proof.text: *Setting up the lifting problem.* Write $\varphi:R\to S$, $\psi:R\to R'$, $\iota:S\to S'$, $s\mapsto s\otimes1$, and $j:R'\to S'$, $r'\mapsto1\otimes r'$; by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property](1) (with $A=S$, $B=R'$) $S'$ is a commutative ring and $\iota$, $j$ are homomorphisms of $R$-algebras, so $\iota\circ\varphi=j\circ\psi$ ($\varphi(r)\otimes1=r(1\otimes1)=1\otimes\psi(r)$); $S'$ is an $R'$-algebra through $j$. To verify [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] for $R'\to S'$ and $\mathfrak n'$, let $D$ be a commutative ring with a ring map $\rho:R'\to D$, $J\subseteq D$ an ideal with $J^2=0$, $q:D\to D/J$ the quotient map, and $g':S'\to D/J$ a homomorphism of $R'$-algebras ($D/J$ an $R'$-algebra through $q\circ\rho$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]) with $g'(\mathfrak n'^k)=0$ for some $k\ge1$; we must find a homomorphism of $R'$-algebras $f':S'\to D$ with $q\circ f'=g'$. Regard $D$ as an $R$-algebra through $\rho\circ\psi$, so $D/J$ is an $R$-algebra through $q\circ\rho\circ\psi$, and put $g=g'\circ\iota:S\to D/J$. It is a ring homomorphism and an $R$-algebra homomorphism: $g(\varphi(r))=g'(j(\psi(r)))=q(\rho(\psi(r)))$, as $g'\circ j=q\circ\rho$ ($g'$ is an $R'$-algebra map). Likewise $\rho:R'\to D$ is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07EG (lemma-base-change-fs, lines 9346-9366): 'Let a solid diagram ... as in Definition 07EB be given'

proof.text: *$g$ is continuous.* $\iota(\mathfrak n^k)\subseteq\mathfrak n'^k$: $\mathfrak n^k$ is generated as an ideal by the products $x_1\cdots x_k$ with $x_i\in\mathfrak n$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and $\iota(x_1\cdots x_k)=\iota(x_1)\cdots\iota(x_k)\in\mathfrak n'^k$ since each $\iota(x_i)\in\mathfrak n'=\mathfrak nS'$; the set $\{z\in S:\iota(z)\in\mathfrak n'^k\}$ contains these generators and is closed under sums and under multiplication by $S$ ($\iota(sz)=\iota(s)\iota(z)$ and $\mathfrak n'^k$ is an ideal of $S'$), so it contains $\mathfrak n^k$. Hence $g(\mathfrak n^k)=g'(\iota(\mathfrak n^k))\subseteq g'(\mathfrak n'^k)=0$ with the same $k\ge1$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07EG (lemma-base-change-fs, lines 9346-9366): 'Then the composition S → S' → A/J is continuous'

proof.text: *The lift over $R$.* By the hypothesis that $S$ is formally smooth over $R$ for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic], applied to the commutative ring $D$ with the ring map $\rho\circ\psi:R\to D$, the ideal $J$ ($J^2=0$) and the $R$-algebra homomorphism $g:S\to D/J$ with $g(\mathfrak n^k)=0$ (Steps 1, 2), there is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $f:S\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07EG (lemma-base-change-fs, lines 9346-9366): 'By assumption the longer dotted arrow exists'

proof.text: *Extension to $S'$.* $f:S\to D$ and $\rho:R'\to D$ are homomorphisms of $R$-algebras into the commutative $R$-algebra $D$ (Steps 1, 3), so [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property](2) (with $A=S$, $B=R'$, $C=D$) gives a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $f':S'=S\otimes_RR'\to D$ with $f'(s\otimes r')=f(s)\rho(r')$, $f'\circ\iota=f$ and $f'\circ j=\rho$. The last equation says that $f'$ is a homomorphism of $R'$-algebras ($R'$ acting on $S'$ through $j$ and on $D$ through $\rho$).

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07EG (lemma-base-change-fs, lines 9346-9366): 'By the universal property of tensor product we obtain the shorter dotted arrow'

proof.text: *$f'$ lifts $g'$.* $q\circ f'$ and $g'$ are homomorphisms of $R$-algebras $S'\to D/J$ ($D/J$ with structure map $q\circ\rho\circ\psi$; $q$ is an $R$-algebra map [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]). They agree after $\iota$: $q\circ f'\circ\iota=q\circ f=g=g'\circ\iota$ (Steps 1, 3, 4); and after $j$: $q\circ f'\circ j=q\circ\rho=g'\circ j$ (Steps 4, 1). By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property](3), $q\circ f'=g'$. So $f'$ is a homomorphism of $R'$-algebras lifting $g'$; as $D$, $\rho$, $J$, $g'$ were arbitrary, $S'$ is formally smooth over $R'$ for the $\mathfrak n'$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. (Stacks leaves this check, the commutativity of the two triangles of the shorter dotted arrow, implicit.)

split_report.summary: Proof written from Stacks More on Algebra 07EG (lemma-base-change-fs, line 9346; tag checked in tags/tags) and its three-sentence proof, against the DAG definition def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic exactly (commutative D with a ring map, J^2 = 0, g(n^k) = 0 for some k ≥ 1). Five steps: (1) the lifting problem over R' and the restricted R-algebra map g = g'∘ι; (2) ι(n^k) ⊆ n'^k, so g kills n^k (elementary); (3) the lift f:S → D from the hypothesis; (4) the R'-algebra map f':S⊗R' → D from f and ρ:R' → D by the pushout property of the tensor product; (5) q∘f' = g' by the uniqueness clause (Stacks leaves this implicit). The existing node lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-base-change-universal-property puts the base ring on the left (S ⊗_R A, S-algebra maps) and would need the swap S⊗R' ≅ R'⊗S; it also gives no ring structure. So one new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property (ring structure on A⊗_R B, existence of h(a⊗b)=f(a)g(b), uniqueness; Algebra.TensorProduct.instCommRing/productMap/ext) was created and added to stmt_deps, since the statement's 'S' is a commutative ring and an R'-algebra' uses its clause (1). Statement unchanged. Mathlib: three search kinds re-done; adic formal smoothness absent, discrete analogue recorded in mathlib_candidate.
